top_findings.title: Standings & team records inflated ~40% by surviving duplicate fixtures
top_findings.evidence: src/store.rs:538 build_unique_match_indices keys dedup on the exact `date`; BR-Football-Dataset.csv records night games in UTC (+1 day) vs Brasileirao_Matches.csv local dates, so off-by-one twins survive (flamengo-cruzeiro B=2019-04-27/F=2019-04-28, csa-flamengo 06-12/06-13, flamengo-internacional 09-25/09-26, flamengo-vasco 11-13/11-14, flamengo-ceara 11-27/11-28). Independent Python reproduction of the store's dedup yields 2019 Flamengo = 53 fixtures, 40W-7D-6L, 127 pts (should be 38 / 28-6-4 / 90); matches _factual.json exactly. factual_accuracy=0.0 in scores.json.
top_findings.suggestion: Dedup on (home_key, away_key, competition, goals) with a +/-1 day date tolerance, or normalize all sources to local match date before keying.

top_findings.title: Team-name normalization both merges distinct clubs and fragments one club
top_findings.evidence: src/normalize.rs:32-72 team_key() strips a trailing state suffix before the alias table, so 'Atletico-MG', 'Atletico-PR' and 'Atletico-GO' ALL collapse to 'atletico', while their long forms map elsewhere ('Atletico Mineiro'->'atletico mg', 'Atletico Paranaense'->'athletico pr', 'Athletico-PR'->'athletico'). 2019 Serie A shows 4 Atletico/Athletico standings rows, expected 2 (_factual.json). One club fragments across rows and three different clubs' matches merge into the 'atletico' bucket.
top_findings.suggestion: Canonicalize with a state-aware alias map (keep the -MG/-PR/-GO distinction) or map every documented variant of each club to a single stable key before dedup and aggregation.
